page: Amazon Web Services m7g.16xlarge is a general-purpose server instance powered by the AWS Graviton3 processor family. It features 64 dedicated physical cores on the arm64 architecture, utilizing AWS Neoverse-V1 cores running at 2.6 GHz. The instance is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 30 Gbps. This instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core and memory performance. The instance achieves a strong rating in stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and Geekbench multi-core scores, while single-core performance remains in the average tier. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with Passmark memory scores reaching the top tier and large-block read-only bandwidth measured at 253.34 GB/sec. Software compilation using Clang also ranks in the top tier. For database workloads, the instance demonstrates strong capabilities, processing 101.03 million Redis SET operations per second and achieving strong throughput in static web serving at 74.33 GB/sec.

While multi-threaded and memory-bound tasks perform well, certain workloads show limitations. For instance, LLM text generation using a small model registers in the poor tier at 13.54 tokens/sec, though medium model text generation is strong. The lack of local NVMe storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, which may impact I/O-heavy operations. Given the balanced vCPU-to-RAM ratio and strong multi-core execution, this instance is suited for application servers, containerized microservices, software compilation pipelines, and database operations.
